turns.text: Hey, you around? Just drifting through. How’s the lazy-day/comfort-game rotation treating you lately?

Hey, yeah—just drifting too. Rotation’s been mostly Stardew on the same forest farm, animals and same romance, basically digital chamomile. Skyrim when I want to wander with no objectives, and Slay the Spire keeps telling me “one more run” like it’s not a lie.

You? Still cycling RimWorld/Darkest Dungeon/PowerWash, or did something new pull you in?

Still the same loop, mostly. PowerWash Simulator has basically become a rain-room: I put on some long drizzle ambient, clean a patio nobody asked for, and my brain just goes idle. RimWorld when I want a colony to slowly turn into a soap opera. Darkest Dungeon only on nights I feel like being a stressed innkeeper. FTL stays in the drawer as a “one jump then bed” lie.

Almost reopened Hades II the other night, but then I just pressure-washed a fence for forty minutes instead.

What about your Stardew run—same spouse as always, or do you at least pretend to court someone new before locking in the sentimental pick?

Same spouse, always. I tell myself this file I’ll finally court someone else, then the first flower dance hits and I’m already walking across town to the same person like it’s muscle memory. At this point it’s less romance and more “yes, this is my Stardew person again.”

I don’t even pretend properly—maybe I’ll gift a couple things to someone else early on, then abandon it instantly. Sentimental pick locked in.

Fence power-washing for forty minutes with drizzle ambient sounds honestly ideal. Was Hades II a real pull, or just the idea of it while the fence was already promising zero stakes?

Honestly Hades II was the idea of a pull, not the pull itself. I like it—it’s sharp, gorgeous, has that “one more chamber” gravity—but it asks for actual hands and attention. The fence asked for nothing except to be hosed, and the drizzle was already going. Zero stakes won.

That’s been the whole rotation lately: whatever lets me keep half a mind in the room and half in static. PowerWash is perfect because it’s just a slow reveal of clean under grime. Almost like erasing, but with water.

Skyrim no-objective wandering is a good call too. Do you ever set out with no plan and end up at some ruin thinking “why am I here?” and then stay anyway? Or is it more “walk, pick flowers, ignore dragon” energy?

Both, honestly. If I’m in Skyrim at night, it’s mostly “walk, pick flowers, ignore dragon” until a ruin appears on the ridge. Then I’ll stand there thinking “why am I here?”—and stay anyway because the music shifts or the torchlight gives it that quiet weight. Less about clearing it, more about being in it for a while. Skyrim aimlessness has a way of feeling like it always knew where you were going, you just didn’t.

Your fence session sounds like the ideal version of that: no plot, just slow transformation. Did Hades II ever get far enough to lock into its rhythm for you, or is it still in the “good but too much hands” category?

Hades II is still in the “good but too much hands” category. I’ll do a few chambers, get into a rhythm, then notice I’m leaning forward like I’m about to solve something—and I gently put it down. It’s not the game’s fault; it’s built to grip. I’m just in a season where I’d rather be held loosely.

Run-based games all lie differently. Slay the Spire lies like “one more run, this deck is special.” Hades II lies like “one more room, you’re already flowing.” Both are trying to make me forget the time. PowerWash doesn’t even bother lying. It just says “the grime is here and then it won’t be,” which is somehow the more honest high-stakes pitch.

Your Skyrim line is going to stick with me: “Skyrim aimlessness has a way of feeling like it always knew where you were going, you just didn’t.” That’s exactly it. It’s not directionless, it’s just not yours.

Is there a particular ruin or spot you always end up at, even when you don’t set out for it? Or is it more whichever torchlight on the ridge says “stay”?

“The grime is here and then it won’t be” is such an honest pitch. It’s not even a challenge; it’s just an invitation to watch effort become absence. No stakes, no trick, just slow before/after.

And yeah, Hades II leaning you forward is exactly it. Some games hold you by the wrist; some hold you by the back of the head. Doesn’t make them bad, just wrong season. I’m in the same season—I want a game that’ll let me look out the window mid-play without punishing the moment.

For Skyrim, I don’t have one fixed ruin, but I have spots that feel pre-set, like the game already queued the mood. The hill above Riverwood when the night track comes in. The road outside Whiterun where the tundra flattens and the streetlight-ish torch glow starts. Bleak Falls Barrow’s exterior specifically—I’ll ride or walk up there, stand by the entrance, and then sometimes not even go in. It’s like the approach was the whole point.

So more “whichever torchlight on the ridge says stay,” but a few of them know my name by now. You ever get that in RimWorld—some map seed or colony spot that keeps pulling you back, not for the story, just because the terrain felt like a place you already lived?

That’s real. RimWorld for me always circles back to a temperate forest seed with a river cutting diagonally, big granite outcrop, and just enough growing season to feel forgiving but not frictionless.
